sec-psych.name: Psychology is the Software; Biology is the Hardware. (the section check after its paragraphs went in)
sec-psych.text:
Psychology is the Software; Biology is the Hardware.

Have you done years of CBT or EMDR and yet you still get triggered and freeze or blow up? One reason to think about, is that standard therapy is trying to rewrite the "code" (your thoughts and behaviors), while the "motherboard" (the brain's physical structure and chemistry) is often overheating or damaged, and code doesn't run well on a motherboard like that. So to address that, I've designed this protocol to go after 5 specific neuro-biological problems (A to E below) before you go working on the psychology (well, alongside).

The "Underpinning" Principle: Bruce Perry compares treating trauma to building a house. Standard CBT & EMDR style therapies attempt to "decorate" the house (changing thoughts/behaviors in the Cortex) while the foundation (the Brainstem) is crumbling, and you can't hang curtains in a collapsing house.

The Modern "Role-Self" vs. The Ancient "True-Self"

Why does the brain build this armor? Psychologist Lindsay Gibson explains that Adult children of emotionally immature parents survive by creating a "Role-Self"--a defensive personality designed to please others and manage the parent's emotions. But we can't just blame our immature parents for this Role Self. It really is true what they say: "It takes a village to raise a child." The modern large society with only one or two people caring for the children is vastly insufficient. As Dr. Bruce Perry explains, our brains evolved in hunter-gatherer bands with a ratio of 4 developmentally mature adults to 1 child. Today, our "enriched" environments offer 1 immature adult to 4 children.

That works out to about one-sixteenth of the grown-ups per child that our brains evolved with (Perry, 2023). So the emptiness you feel (the "Void") is real, since it's what that missing company feels like. Once you've de-armored, going back to a lonely life will tend to feel worse than it did with the armor on. So gather a tribe of people you're close to and who you hang with on most days, or you'll eventually put the armor back on just to get through the loneliness.

We grew up building a "role-self" to please and manage the people around us. And the role-self psychology gets locked in physiologically by Dopamine and DeltaFosB, which also underlie addictions, so it's a vicious cycle as both create the other. That's why I built this protocol, to go after the chemistry holding the false persona in place, so the person you were before the trauma (your "True-Self") can come back out.

Neurological De-Armoring is about fixing the underpinnings, not redecorating. It's a protocol that works like a metabolic solvent that softens the "concrete" in the brainstem by using Glutamate modulation and supplementing Ketones (BHB, which block HDACs) so we can dig under the house and pour a new foundation, and eventually work on the psychology upstairs.

The Anti-Breakthrough (Micro-Dosing): A brain stuck in alarm can often take in healing work for only a few seconds at a time, Perry finds. So for now we have to give up on the hour-long breakthrough that therapy aims for, since an hour spent working on the trauma itself overwhelms an armored nervous system more than it heals it. Instead, this protocol works in doses of a few seconds, which is another dimension of micro-dosing.

In practice, I'd do something like 30 seconds of slow breathing, 20 times a day.
